newsitem.title: USA: Genetics hemophilia drug gets FDA panel ok.
newsitem.headline: Genetics hemophilia drug gets FDA panel ok.

text.p: Genetics Institute Inc said Thursday that a U.S. Food and Drug Administration panel recommended the agency license BeneFIX, the company's blood clotting therapy for hemophilia B.
Genetics said the FDA will consider the recommendation in its review of BeneFix's application but said it does not know if or when the therapy wiil get regulatory approval.
The panel included in its findings a recommendation that Genetics conduct post-licensure studies to supplement the data presented to them, the company said.
Genetics Institute shares gained 1-3/4 Thursday afternoon to 63-1/4.
Hemophilia B is an inherited disorder that almost exclusively affects males. It arises from a deficiency or defect in Factor IX, a protein involved in blood clotting.
The disorder affects about 7,000 people in North America, Europe and Japan and about 3,000 in the U.S., the company said.
Genetics Institute said more than 20 percent of U.S. hemophilia patients are infected with HIV because of viral contamination from plasma-derived clotting therapies.
The company said BeneFIX is made without added blood or plasma products, eliminating blood-borne viral contamination.
